notes: The vendored source is the standard library's net/http/internal/http2, resolved from $(go env GOROOT), not a module cache: as of Go 1.27 that package is the source of truth and golang.org/x/net/http2 only receives critical fixes.
Re-basing therefore means re-copying from a Go toolchain, and base_go/min_go move with it. A machine with a different toolchain re-bases against that toolchain's sources.
Every site that edits an upstream-owned file leaves a '// fork: <site-id>' marker at the edit point; scripts/minimal-diff-check.sh fails when one is missing.

sites.summary: Only the client-side closure of the standard library package is vendored.
anchors: files.allowlist, files.exclude and files.nested are the complete rule.
A file is needed when the vendored package fails to compile without it.
invariants: Every allowlist entry exists in the toolchain's net/http/internal/http2.
No upstream test file is vendored.
Server-only files (server.go, write.go, writesched*.go, ciphers.go, gotrack.go) stay out; the client subset compiles without them.
Dropped packages stay importable from the standard library, e.g. hpack comes from golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack.

sites.summary: The copied packages keep their import paths rewritten, and net/http/internal references are localised.
anchors: Any import of a net/http/internal/... path.
The bare net/http/internal import used for the ErrAbortHandler, ErrBodyNotAllowed, ErrSkipAltProtocol, ErrRequestCanceled and DetectContentType symbols.
invariants: No file under http2/ imports a net/http/internal/... path.

The standard library avoids net/http only to break an import cycle; the fork is a separate module and may import it, so the sentinels become http.ErrAbortHandler, http.ErrBodyNotAllowed and http.ErrSkipAltProtocol.
ErrRequestCanceled is internal to the client, so a local errors.New replaces it; its identity never crosses the package boundary.
Every internal package the vendored files import has a matching copy under http2/internal/.

sites.summary: api.go loses the server-facing surface and initialises the two variables net/http normally fills in.

targets.symbol: ServerConfig, Handler, ResponseWriter, PushOptions, ServerRequest, ConnState

anchors: Type declarations after TransportConfig that reference net.Conn, log.Logger or multipart.Form.
NoBody and LocalAddrContextKey, which net/http assigns into the standard library copy at init time.
invariants: ClientRequest, ClientResponse, Header and TransportConfig stay.
NoBody and LocalAddrContextKey are initialised from net/http in the fork's own init.
The remaining file needs no net/multipart/log imports.

sites.summary: configFromServer is dropped because the server half of the package is not vendored.
anchors: Helper taking a ServerConfig and returning Config.
invariants: configFromTransport is kept unchanged apart from its fork marker.
The Config struct stays field-for-field identical to net/http.HTTP2Config; the fork converts between them in transportConfig.HTTP2Config.

sites.summary: Server-side request decoding is dropped from the copied httpcommon package.
anchors: Symbols at the end of the upstream file used only by server.go.
invariants: Removing them keeps the package compiling without the server files.
Nothing in the vendored client subset references these symbols.

sites.summary: Transport carries the fork's Options, and Options carries the uTLS config and the dialer.
anchors: The Transport struct, which upstream declares as t1 plus connPool plus transportTestHooks.
Options with HeaderOrder, PHeaderOrder, Settings, WindowSizeIncrement, PriorityParams, GetTlsClientHelloSpec, TLSClientConfig.
invariants: Transport.opt is read by newClientConn, by the header-writing path and by dialTLSWithContext.
Options.TLSClientConfig holds the uTLS config because the vendored Transport has no TLS fields of its own.
Options.dialContext is unexported: configureTransports fills it from the net/http Transport.

sites.summary: transportConfig adapts the net/http Transport to the vendored TransportConfig interface.
anchors: The vendored TransportConfig interface: MaxHeaderListSize, MaxResponseHeaderBytes, DisableCompression, DisableKeepAlives, ExpectContinueTimeout, ResponseHeaderTimeout, IdleConnTimeout, HTTP2Config.
net/http's own transportConfig in src/net/http/http2.go, which merges http.Transport fields the same way.
invariants: Every method delegates to the http.Transport the fork is installed on, so caller settings keep working.
HTTP2Config converts http.HTTP2Config to Config directly: upstream keeps the two field-for-field identical.
MaxHeaderListSize returns zero because net/http has no such field; the limit comes from MaxResponseHeaderBytes.

sites.summary: The fork translates between net/http and the vendored ClientRequest/ClientResponse types.
anchors: The vendored ClientRequest and ClientResponse types, which exist so the standard library package does not import net/http.
net/http's own adapter in src/net/http/http2.go (http2RoundTrip), which the fork cannot import.
ErrNoCachedConn and isNoCachedConnError, which net/http maps to http.ErrSkipAltProtocol so it can fall back to its own dial path.
invariants: roundTripHTTP keeps Request, TLS, Trailer, ContentLength and Uncompressed on the response.
noDialH2RoundTripper returns http.ErrSkipAltProtocol when no conn is cached, never an error.
registerHTTPSProtocol converts RegisterProtocol's panic into an error, as the old x/net transport did.

sites.summary: ConfigureTransport and ConfigureTransports are fork-only: the standard library package has no net/http integration of its own.
anchors: The net/http Transport the caller passes in.
NewTransport(transportConfig{...}), which builds the vendored Transport together with its connection pool.
invariants: The exported signature takes variadic Options: ConfigureTransport(t1 *http.Transport, opt ...Options) error.
The fork transport is built through NewTransport so the connection pool is never nil.
t1.DialTLSContext is set so every h2 dial goes through uTLS rather than net/http's own TLS.
Both TLSNextProto entries, h2 and unencrypted_http2, route through upgradeFn.
The https alt protocol is registered so net/http hands h2 requests to the fork.

sites.summary: dialTLSWithContext is rewritten to handshake through uTLS.
anchors: The vendored method that wraps tls.Dialer{Config: cfg}.DialContext and returns cn.(*tls.Conn).
dialTLS immediately above it, which calls ConnectionState() on the result and checks NegotiatedProtocol.
invariants: The return type is *utls.UConn, which satisfies the dialTLS caller's use of ConnectionState().
The uTLS handshake runs on the conn from Options.dialContext, so the caller's dialer and timeouts still apply.
Options.GetTlsClientHelloSpec nil means HelloGolang; otherwise HelloCustom plus ApplyPreset.
A failed handshake closes the underlying conn.

sites.summary: newClientConn takes SETTINGS, the connection WINDOW_UPDATE and PRIORITY frames from Options.
anchors: The vendored method building a ClientConn, writing clientPreface and then WriteSettings of a slice derived from the TransportConfig.
The connectionStater branch that stores cc.tlsState.
invariants: Every SETTINGS id/val pair from Options.Settings reaches the wire in the caller's order.
Options.WindowSizeIncrement replaces the TransportConfig value as the connection WINDOW_UPDATE when non-zero.
Each Options.PriorityParams entry becomes one PRIORITY frame.
A negotiated protocol other than NextProtoTLS returns the ClientConn instead of failing.
cc.tlsState stays nil: net/http holds the forged conn, not the uTLS one.

sites.summary: encodeRequestHeaders carries Options so header order reaches the encoder.
anchors: The helper that builds EncodeHeadersParam from a ClientRequest.
Its single caller in writeRequest, which passes cs.requestedGzip and cc.peerMaxHeaderListSize.
invariants: The call site passes cc.t.opt.
EncodeHeadersParam keeps AddGzipHeader, PeerMaxHeaderListSize and DefaultUserAgent unchanged and adds HeaderOrder and PHeaderOrder.

anchors: Pseudo-header emission that upstream writes as :authority, :method, :path, :scheme in a fixed order.
Loop over req.Header that upstream writes as "for k, vv := range req.Header".
invariants: With PHeaderOrder set, pseudo headers are emitted in exactly that order; unset reproduces upstream order.
With HeaderOrder set, listed headers come first in listed order and unlisted ones follow lexicographically.
Name lookups are case-insensitive: the sorter compares strings.ToLower(key) against HeaderOrder entries.
Header names are still lowercased by LowerHeader before they reach the wire.
The fork adds the net/http import that http.MethodGet needs.

sites.summary: hackTlsConn forges a crypto/tls.Conn wrapping the uTLS conn so net/http's TLSNextProto path accepts it.
anchors: reflect.TypeOf(new(cryptotls.Conn)).Elem() field offsets collected for conn, config, clientProtocol and isHandshakeComplete.
unsafe.Pointer arithmetic writing those private fields on a freshly allocated crypto/tls.Conn.
invariants: A field name that disappears or changes type makes this site BROKEN, never silently skipped: the offsets are what make net/http hand the conn to the h2 RoundTripper.
Only conns whose negotiated protocol is NextProtoTLS are wrapped; anything else is returned unchanged.
isHandshakeComplete is set through Store, not by assigning a sync/atomic.Bool value, so go vet stays clean.
This site disappears only if the fork stops using TLSNextProto and owns the https path itself.

sites.summary: The unencrypted-h2 handoff unwraps net/http's TLSNextProto conn.
anchors: net/http wraps a cleartext conn in a *tls.Conn implementing UnencryptedNetConn() net.Conn before calling TLSNextProto["unencrypted_http2"].
The x/net implementation of the same helper, which the standard library package does not carry.
invariants: The parameter type is net.Conn, not *crypto/tls.Conn.
A conn without UnencryptedNetConn is an error, not a silent fallback.

sites.summary: Every edit to an upstream-owned file is marked with a // fork: comment naming its site.

targets.symbol: every site declared with change: rewritten in place
every site declared with an upstream-owned target

anchors: A comment of the form "// fork: <site-id>" immediately above the edit.
invariants: No large commented-out upstream function body exists anywhere in http2/.
scripts/minimal-diff-check.sh fails when an upstream-owned site has no marker.

sites.summary: The golden fingerprint and the net/http wiring are pinned offline.
anchors: goldenAkamaiFingerprint constant that mirrors the live assertion in patch_test.go.
The profile in the tests, settings and window increment and header order, must stay identical to the profile in patch_test.go.
TestEndToEndOverPipe serves one request over net.Pipe with a hand written responder; net.Pipe has no buffer, so the responder must keep reading while a separate goroutine writes.
invariants: The tests never open a network connection.
The golden string equals SETTINGS|WINDOW_UPDATE|priority|pseudo-header codes.
When the live profile changes, the tests change together.
TestHackTlsConn drives a real uTLS handshake over net.Pipe against a crypto/tls server, so a Go release that renames the unexported crypto/tls.Conn fields fails offline.
TestEndToEndOverPipe asserts the 200 response plus the SETTINGS and header order seen on the wire, which proves net/http routes to TLSNextProto["h2"] rather than its bundled HTTP/2.
